claims.statement: CI seals both assembly-qualified targets into one immutable complete-product record with exact source, producer attempt, toolchain inputs, asset identities, and independently hashed Control bytes. Schema 2 COMPONENT_ASSEMBLY replaces the removed native test harness receipt. Detached installed-product receipts are joined without rewriting the record; sealing alone does not establish installed acceptance.

The retained component-candidate reuse path admits source-tree equality and exact payload digests while preserving original producer and merged revision in promotion evidence. That legacy component candidate is not the complete two-target product used by current developer publication.
Component release admission checks the selected component and revision, exact asset inventory, checksums, byte counts, and archive contents.

Published preview discovery keeps at most five immutable products ordered by proven main ancestry. Product publication converts the discovery window to product-only entries without deleting old releases or pins. Guarded publication changes the catalog and pointer together after asset admission and rereads after contention.

For published products, the managed installer consumes one captured complete-product selection, rechecks its exact build-record bytes and both CI targets under schema 2/3, and admits the selected target archive bytes, native receipt, composed inventory and component compatibility before activation. Legacy main component pairs reject; stable selection requires an exact product mapping.

Developer promotion admits successful main push or manual CI runs only when the validation record matches the exact producer event and identity. Manual CI selects full validation and needs explicit developer publication.

Installed-product acceptance requires a sealed baseline with a different actual target composition, not prior publication. New assembly-qualified baselines also need installed acceptance, while legacy native-qualified baselines retain their original admission contract. CI verifies the exact baseline record, producer attempt, and successful sealing job even if a later job failed.

The installed-product probe upgrades a baseline, removes it, installs the fresh candidate, and verifies passive discovery before three simultaneous public first queries. Schema 2 installed receipts require all 18 cases, including caller provenance, Java references, unknown-result rejection, Linux runtime libraries and answering-Host identity, stop cleanup, and edit re-analysis. Legacy v1 retains its 12 cases only with component-native evidence. Source and receipt checks do not establish native execution.
Linux composition starts alongside source validation, but sealing requires successful source work and both qualified targets; independent compilation cannot bypass a failed source check.

Fresh Mac complete-product composition admits the same-run, same-attempt assembled release through revision, tree, version, digest, platform, and toolchain checks instead of rebuilding Control. A rejected artifact fails; the separately selected reused PR candidate path keeps independent compilation when no same-attempt native release exists.

Local schema 4 product records retain one supported LOCAL-provenance target without CI run identities; installed decoding admits them, but published decoding and the CI target-record join reject them. A local build export does not establish published-product or detached installed-product acceptance qualification.
